prerequisites: Electrical Circuits Theory I and II

learning_outcomes.text: Design electrical systems and their components.
Diagnosis, troubleshooting and maintenance of electrical systems and components.
Identification of the objectives to be achieved, available resources, conditions to complete them, working stages, working times, associated deadlines and risks.

Analyse the variations of monitored parameters, useful for optimizing the process and designing microwave ovens, starting from the preconditions imposed by each product subject to industrial microwave processing.

syllabus_topics: Properties of dielectrics. Techniques for measuring complex dielectric constant. Variation of complex permittivity depending on humidity, temperature and frequency. Quality factor analysis. Agents and catalysts

Theoretical aspects of volume heating. Dissipated power. Propagation factor and penetration depth. Specific heat. Increase temperature factor. Heat and mass transfer phenomena. Penetration depth. Leaks in the walls of the oven

Single-mode resonant cavities. The modes generated in the cavity and the quality factor. Impedance adaptation. Determining the parameters by measuring the transmitted power or the reflected power. Rectangular and cylindrical cavities. Coupling slots. Energy transfer and efficiency in a resonant microwave oven.

Multimode applicators. Field distribution and uniform heating. The quality factor, the intensity of the electric field and the currents in the walls, the power density. Choice of material for the walls of the applicator. Doors and locking mechanisms.
Wave applicators with conveyor belt. Parallel plane waves. Wave guides. Mutual impedance. Voltage Standing Wave Ratio S. Examples of conveyor belt applicators
Special applicator structures. TE10n applicator with two cavities. Applicator: periodic, rectangular TEM, with ridge, disc, dielectric, mobile resonant, spiral, radiant, ellipsoidal and spherical
General aspects of the microwave heating circuit, gas discharge phenomena and pressure processing.
Pressure microwave processing of sensitive materials at high temperature
Automatic control, adjustment and adaptation of the drying process.
Hybrid systems in industrial applications that use microwave technologies
Safety rules adopted for microwave installations
Occupational Safety and Health Administration – technical instruction for microwaves systems installations in the laboratory
Analysis of the component parts and the operation mode of the laboratory installation for microwave drying or treatment of dielectric materials
Measurement and interpretation of process parameters at microwave drying of granular products
Measurement and interpretation of process parameters at mixed microwave / hot air drying of granular products
Analysis of the component parts and of the operation of the laboratory installation for soil decontamination. Measurement and interpretation of results
Measurement and interpretation of process parameters to study the influence of high frequency electromagnetic field on soil seed germination processes
Analysis of the component parts and the operation of the laboratory installation for extracting oils from seeds. Measurement and interpretation of results
Measurement and interpretation of process parameters for the extraction of beta-carotene from vegetables (carrots)
Analysis of the component parts and the operation of the laboratory installation for the extraction of oils from vegetable substrate. Measurement and interpretation of results
Measurement and interpretation of results in the extraction of oils from the floral substrate.
Analysis of the component parts and the operation of the laboratory installation for the study of microwave susceptor ceramic materials. Measurement and interpretation of results

Analysis of the component parts and the operation of the laboratory reactor in the microwave field in order to obtain hybrid materials (conductive, semiconductor or dielectric polymers) by spray pyrolysis processes. Measurement and interpretation of results
Knowledge verification
assessment_rules: The final grade (N) is calculated as 0.8 times the Exam grade (Ex) plus 0.2 times the Laboratory grade (L). To obtain credits, both the final grade (N) and the Laboratory grade (L) must be equal to or greater than 5.
